displayText: Squash by three, and every run shrinks to a third, so every slope is three times as steep. The derivative of e to the three x is three e to the three x. What about a negative number, like e to the minus two x? The minus also flips the curve in the y axis, so it falls instead of rising. Every uphill tangent becomes a downhill one, just as steep. So the gradient is minus two times the height. The height stays positive, because e to any power is positive. It's only the slope that turns negative.
